maml:description.maml:para: Retrieves Azure AD application (Service Principal) information from Microsoft Graph API.

Gets comprehensive information about Azure AD/Entra Service Principals (Enterprise Apps) with multi-source activity analysis for security assessment. Includes display names, owners, client IDs, credential details (for owned apps), source, and comprehensive activity tracking across: - User sign-ins (interactive and non-interactive) - Service principal operations and API usage - Delegated access through Azure Portal and other Microsoft services - Application authentication activity and management operations This provides complete "Days Since Last Activity" calculations for identifying unused/dead applications. Uses helper functions in the Private folder for data retrieval steps.

Optional. The display name of a specific Service Principal (Enterprise App) to retrieve. If not specified, all are returned. Note: Filtering is applied *after* retrieving all SPs due to the need for expanded properties.
Optional. Filters the Service Principals based on their type. Valid values are 'All', 'AppRegistrations', 'EnterpriseApps', 'MicrosoftApps', and 'ManagedIdentities'.

Controls how much supporting data is collected: - Full : current behaviour (delegated perms, owners, comprehensive activity) – requires broad Graph permissions - Light : skips delegated permission grants and comprehensive activity; still collects owners - Minimal : skips delegated permission grants, owners and comprehensive activity (suitable for expiry-only monitoring)
Switch parameter. When specified, includes detailed credential information (from Get-MyAppCredentials, requires corresponding Application object) in the output objects under the 'Keys' property.

Switch parameter. When specified, includes detailed authentication method information for the LastSignInMethod field. NOTE: This parameter now has limited impact since comprehensive activity tracking is enabled by default. The primary difference is that it fetches authentication method details (e.g., "Password", "MFA", "Certificate"). For most security assessments, this parameter is optional as the comprehensive activity data provides sufficient information. WARNING: This can be slower for large tenants as it downloads recent sign-in logs to extract authentication methods.

Switch parameter. When specified, includes real-time sign-in logs for enhanced activity accuracy. WARNING: This can be very expensive for large tenants (100k+ users) as it downloads recent sign-in logs for all applications. The aggregated data (default) is usually sufficient for security assessment and is much faster. Only use this for small tenants or when you need the most current sign-in data.
Forces comprehensive activity analysis to be skipped regardless of DetailLevel.
Forces delegated permission grants to be skipped regardless of DetailLevel.

maml:description.maml:para: Reads safe renewal status or loads the active certificate for Connect-MgGraph.

Reads a profile protected for the current Windows account. Ordinary output contains identifiers, public thumbprints, expiry and lifecycle state. AsCertificate explicitly loads a private credential into this process; keep it alive for the SDK connection and dispose it after disconnecting. No Graph connection, certificate-store import or credential write occurs.
Returns the active X509Certificate2 with an ephemeral private key instead of status metadata.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets device information from Microsoft Graph API.
Retrieves device information from Microsoft Graph API and formats it for easy consumption. Allows filtering by device type (Hybrid, AzureAD joined, etc.) and synchronization status.
When specified, enriches devices with Windows Autopilot identity metadata.

Full retains the complete device information. Lifecycle omits registered owners. Computer returns only the dates, identifiers, and owner fields needed for computer inventory correlation. Computer requests retry individual Graph pages. Owner continuations are read when present; a possibly truncated owner expansion makes the inventory fail.

Uses retrying Graph pages for any property set and writes page and record counts to the information stream. If a page remains incomplete, no inventory is returned. The default non-Computer route retains SDK enumeration.
Returns only synchronized devices when specified (OnPremisesSyncEnabled is true).
Filter devices by type. Valid values are 'Hybrid AzureAD', 'AzureAD joined', 'AzureAD registered', and 'Not available'.

maml:description.maml:para: Retrieves selected directory user data, extensions and optional manager details through the Graph SDK.

Returns plain records for automation without license, role or report enrichment. Reads every list page before emitting records, so a failed page cannot yield an apparently complete inventory. Id is always selected. Custom directory extension properties are lifted from the SDK's AdditionalProperties. extensionAttribute1 through extensionAttribute15 select and flatten the corresponding on-premises extension attribute; explicitly requesting OnPremisesExtensionAttributes preserves that nested value.
Eventual consistency for an advanced list query. Graph may also require CountVariable for the filter.
SDK variable name receiving the matching collection count in global scope. Enables eventual consistency. The count describes all matching users, not just a projection or a partial page.
OData filter forwarded to the SDK list query. Construct literal values with OData quote escaping.
Includes a nested Manager record with identity, employee ID, name, UPN, mail and synchronization state, or null. Manager expansion cannot be combined with advanced count/eventual-consistency queries.

Minimum number of users required in a complete list response. Defaults to 0. An undersized response terminates before any records are emitted. The caller chooses the threshold for its selected filter. This counts returned users, before caller-specific indexing or validation of mail and employee IDs.
Fields to return. Defaults to Id, DisplayName, UserPrincipalName, Mail, AccountEnabled and UserType. Id is included even when omitted. Selecting Manager also enables manager expansion.

maml:description.maml:para: Advances opt-in application certificate renewal using the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK.

Renews the enrolled software certificate when due, verifies a fresh token using the replacement, activates its protected profile reference, and retires the previous key after overlap. Run maintenance in a dedicated PowerShell process, not parallel SDK runspaces. After Action Activated, load the new active certificate and reconnect long-running SDK consumers. A missing or ambiguous replacement keeps the hold.

Accepts one or more records with EmailAddress, optional DisplayName, SendInvitationMessage, InviteRedirectUrl, UserType, ResetRedemption, InvitedUserId and opaque Context. CSV Boolean text True/False is supported; email delivery defaults to false. Redirect defaults to myapps.microsoft.com. Returns one ordered outcome per input. Only explicit HTTP 429 responses are retried. Lost responses, malformed successes, duplicate receipts, HTTP 408 and server failures require reconciliation, not replay. Throwing prevents that dispatch and terminates processing. Correlation IDs are not server-side idempotency keys.
